## VARIATION OF PUBLIC SECTOR AWARDS [2026] TASICFB 2

## REASONS FOR DECISION

## HOBART, 25 FEBRUARY 2026

**[1]** On 28 November 2025, the Tasmanian Trades and Labor Council (TTLC) lodged an 
application seeking to:

• Vary the Tasmanian Minimum Wage for an adult in full-time employment specified 
by s 47AB of the Act by an increase of 3.5% to become $948.00 per week effective 
from the first full pay period commencing on or after 1 August 2025, and to increase 
the minimum wage contained in the awards to the same level.

• Increase to $109 per week the minimum wage payable to persons engaged under 
the supported wage system, effective from the first full pay period commencing on 
or after 1 August 2025.

• Increase by 3.5% the wage payable to persons engaged under the Tasmanian State 
Service National Training Wage Award, effective from the first full pay period 
commencing on or after 1 August 2025.

**[2]** The matter proceeded to hearing on 16 February 2026. Tessa McLaughlin appeared
on behalf of the Tasmanian Trades and Labor Council (TTLC), Elizabeth Roberts and Jayne 
Lockley appeared on behalf of the Minister administering the State Service Act 2000 (MASSA), 
Lilli Midgley appeared for the Community and Public Sector Union (State Public Services 
Federation Tasmania) Inc, James Milligan appeared for Health Services Union, Tasmania 
Branch and Leigh Hills for United Firefighters Union of Australia, Tasmania Branch.

**[3]** In addition, the following organisations provided written consent to the application: 
Governor in Council; the Official Secretary, the Police Association of Tasmania, the United 
Workers’ Union and the Australian Education Union, Tasmanian Branch.

**[4]** Ms McLaughlin provided submissions in support of the application. In her written 
submissions she said:

“…

• The Fair Work Commission’s annual wage review raised the national minimum wage 
by 3.5% from $24.10 an hour to $24.95 an hour or $948.00 for a 38-hour week 
commencing 1 July 2025. It also raised the supported wage system minimum to $109.00 
per week.

• In recent years, the Tasmanian Industrial Commission has aligned our minimum wage 
with the adjustments determined by Fair Work and we submit that this remains a fair and 
reasonable way to maintain the Tasmanian minimum wage.

• Cost of living pressures on modern award-reliant employees were a primary 
consideration in the Fair Work Commission’s determination that this level of rise was 
appropriate. We note that here in Tasmania, wages continue to trail the national average. 
The result has been that living standards for employee’s dependent on modern award 
wages have been squeezed and the low paid have experienced greater difficulty in 
meeting their everyday needs

• We also note the Commission must have regard to the public interest in exercising its 
jurisdiction to determine the minimum weekly wage and to vary the Awards. It is our submission that it is in the public interest to increase Tasmania’s minimum wage in line 
with the national minimum wage order to maintain a relevant minimum safety net.

• In relation to the supported wage system, custom and practice has seen the rate vary 
in line with the national supported wage minimum and consistent with income tests for 
pensions set by the Department of Social Services. These have been published and we 
seek that the supported wage minimum be increased to $109.00 per week.

• With respect to the Tasmanian State Service National Training Wage Award, we note 
that clause 12(d) of this Award provides that all wage rates are to be adjusted, effective 
from 1 August, by the same percentage that the Tasmanian Minimum Wage increases, 
as determined in accordance with section 47AB of the Industrial Relations Act 1984. 
Accordingly, the application before you includes an increase of 3.5% to the wage rates
in this Award.

**[5]** The parties who appeared endorsed the submissions made by the TTLC and agreed the 
variations are in accordance with the public interest. As noted, all written submissions received 
also supported the Application.

**[6]** Pursuant to s 47AB of the Act we determine that the Tasmanian minimum wage for an 
adult in full-time employment will be $948.00 per week effective from the first full pay period 
commencing on or after 1 August 2025.

**[7]** Awards containing a supported wage clause will be varied to reflect the new supported
wage of $109.00 per week effective from the first full pay period commencing on or after 1 August
2025. We note that this rate has historically been set at an income level which does not
compromise benefits received under the Department of Social Services pensions.

**[8]** The training wage is also increased by 3.5% for those covered by the Tasmania State 
Service National Training Wage Award.

**[9]** Pursuant to s 23 of the Act, awards containing minimum wage and supported wage 
clauses will be varied to reflect this decision.

**[10]** All Award variations arising from this decision will be effective from FFPPOA 1 August
2025.

**[11]** Orders arising from this decision will be settled by the Registrar with recourse to the
Deputy President.

THE STAMP OF THE TASMANIAN INDUSTRIAL COMMISSION
TASMANIA
Neroli Ellis
Deputy President
